groups.passage: Climbing the most difficult mountains requires a very special mental condition. [[21]] the climber is doing something very difficult, everything that he or she sees, hears, or [[22]] must come together to help in the work of climbing. All of the parts of the body work together smoothly and quietly [[23]] each part feels what is happening in the other parts. There is no room for thinking about what time it is, or about how one looks. [[24]] thinking must focus on what is happening at that moment, and the mind and the body become one. Only by entering this quiet mental state [[25]] a climber really do his or her best.

groups.passage:
I wonder how often your family has bought new furniture, curtains or kitchen equipment and then wondered how to <u>dispose of</u> the old items that still have quite a lot of life left in them.
It was in response to this situation that The Carpenters’ Shop was opened in the town of Walsall, Staffordshire. Run by a team of church volunteers, the shop will collect any surplus, good-quality items and store them until they can be redistributed to the people who are needing those particular things.
Many have been helped through the scheme, including single parents, disabled people and the elderly, and those who have lost all their household possessions through a disaster such as a house fire.
It’s an admirable project, and it is worth finding out if a similar one operates in your hometown. Participation costs the donor nothing and can make such a difference to others.

groups.passage:
What can you do if you ‘lose’ the data from your disks? To find an expert, who would recover the lost information for you, is probably the easiest solution. Jack Olson is one of these experts. Jack and a few of his friends set up a company called “Jack’s Disk Doctor Service” in 1984. They work from home and give all the money they earn to charity. The fees are always the same, no matter how precious the data on the disk is. Some people, however, are so grateful that they send extra money to Jack or to the charities his company supports. One oil company offered him $2000 for his help and an architect even sent him a blank check.
It would be difficult to put a value on the things <u>rescued</u> by the Disk Doctor. There have been disks containing medical research, television scripts, manuscripts of whole books, a lawyer’s papers for a court case, and even Margaret Thatcher’s travel plan for a visit to eastern Europe. For this last case, Jack had to go in person to Thatcher's office ‘for security reasons’!
Disks are usually sent to the Disk Doctor by post, but sometimes people are in such a hurry that they cannot wait for the mail to come. For example, some radio scripts had to be rushed by taxi to Jack’s house because they were needed for broadcasting the next day. When the material has been recovered, the disk is returned to the sender with a diagnosis and a prescription for avoiding the problem in the future. One grateful client, an author, put a “thank you” to Jack in the front of his book. “Jack saved me from a heart attack,” he wrote. “But,” says Jack, “most people don’t take any notice of the doctor’s advice!”

options.C: The architect always followed the doctor's advice

groups.passage:
Do you know the meaning of the word “relationship”? Here is an easy way of understanding it. Whenever two people come together, even for a brief moment, they exchange looks, feelings, thoughts, ideas, and energy. Their relationship is how they interact with each other. Everything that happens in the world happens through relationships. We human beings need to love and be loved, and this will come from our relationship with others. Accordingly, anyone who wishes to love and be loved will want to establish lasting relationships.
Here are a few <u>tips</u> to help us create enduring relationships. First, know our steps. The relationship between two people is like the art of dancing. Before we can dance with a partner, we need to be able to dance by ourselves. We need to feel the rhythm of the music, hear how it inspires us to move and learn our unique style of movement and expression. Second, trust. As the key building block for enduring relationships, trust is a bond that evolves as two persons get to know each other and experience safety in opening their hearts. Trust develops when we respect each other’s needs and develop a history of common experience and caring. Third, be intimate. While intimacy is often limited to the sexual bond, we can be intimate with many people without sexuality. That is, by relating heart to heart. We need to be seen and known by another person. In this way, intimacy enables us to thrive and grow. Lastly, treat relationship as an organism. A new relationship is like an embryo that requires time, care and attention to grow into whatever may evolve. In our proper relationship with others, we will be known and seen for who we are, and love will come out of the seeing and the knowing.

questions.stem: The author writes the above passage chiefly to ______.

options.A: encourage readers to build blocks for intimacy
options.B: tell readers that things happen through feelings
options.D: urge readers to become expert dancers

questions.stem: The word tips in the second paragraph refers to ______.

refers_to.note: 原卷選文畫底線（題幹為粗體）

options.B: “Trust” blocks the way to durable relationships.
options.C: If you do not dance, you cannot establish relationships.
options.D: Exposure of one’s inner thoughts is essential for enduring relationships.

groups.passage:
Penghu, Nov.24—Two Russians, a father and a son, were rescued Saturday near the Penghu Islands off southwestern Taiwan after their sailboat broke down and began drifting.
Medvedev Vladimir, 43, and his son, Maxsine, 14, sailed from an unnamed eastern Russian seaport on August 18, to begin an ambitious around-the-world cruise.
Their voyage, down the coastline of northeastern mainland China, through the East China Sea, then down the Taiwan Strait and into the South China Sea, had been smooth until four days ago when the mainsail of their twin-mast sailboat “Kawasaki” was smashed by strong winds on the high seas.
The father-and-son team started the inboard engine. However, after less than two days, the engine broke down.
Near the “black ditch” of Penghu, battered by winds of up to 70 knots, the rear sail was torn into shreds. The rudder also stopped responding.
Surprised by the father and son’s “pale faces” and their battered vessel, the Penghu police and fishers in Paisha rescued them. Speaking only limited English, the Vladimirs spent five hours trying to explain their presence.
It is not immediately known whether the “Kawasaki” can be repaired on the fishing island of Penghu, or when the Vladimirs will be able to set off again and continue their around-the-world voyage.

questions.stem: What was the purpose of the voyage of the Vladimirs?

options.C: To look for their lost family members.
options.D: To start the inboard engine of their vessel.

questions.stem: Which course (direction) did the Vladimirs take to get to Penghu?
When did the “Kawasaki” first get into trouble during the voyage?

options.A: Less than two days after departure from Russia.
options.B: About four days before the inboard engine was started.
options.C: After it had sailed from Russia for more than three months.
options.D: Only after it drifted to Paisha County of the Penghu Islands.

questions.stem: What did the Vladimirs decide to do after they were rescued?

options.A: To stay in Penghu and do some fishing.
options.B: To sell the boat and return to Russia.
options.C: To repair the boat and sail back to Russia.
options.D: They had not made any decision yet.

tags.topic: a Russian father and son rescued near Penghu during an around-the-world voyage

groups.passage:
Do you know that happy folks recover from illness much more readily than people who are depressed and always complaining?
The old sages always used to say that laughter was the best medicine—indeed, better than medicine.
Someone else remarked that “a merry heart does good, like medicine”—and infectious laughter is often catching. Don’t you find it so? I like the anonymous verse which sums it all up:
When wholesome laughter fills the air,
Some ills will soon depart;
For laughter is good medicine
That helps to cheer the heart.

sections.title: 貳、英文作文
sections.instructions:
說明：1.請依下列提示寫一篇英文作文在「答案卷」上。
2.文長以120字左右為原則，共20分。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem:
提示：
你同意 “Laughter is better than medicine” 這種說法嗎？以你自己或親朋好友的經驗或你所知道的故事為例，加以說明。你的論點無論是正面或是反面都不會影響你的得分。

extraction.method: 官方 Word 版（paper-2.doc → soffice 轉 docx → python-docx，依 run 的底線屬性辨識空格與畫底線字）取文字，與 pdftotext -layout 題本逐字比對（除換行外完全一致）；以 Read 逐頁檢視題本 PDF 影像（8 頁，含封面）確認版面、段落、粗體／斜體／底線；答案檔為國文、英文、數學合併的掃描檔（無文字層），以 pdftoppm 250dpi 轉圖並裁切英文欄，用 Read 看影像逐題抄錄。；查證者獨立複核：answer.pdf 以 pdftoppm 300dpi 轉圖裁切英文欄，用 Read 看影像重新逐題抄錄第1–55題並與 JSON 程式比對（55/55 一致）；Word 版轉 docx 後以 python-docx 讀出（含底線／粗體 run），與 JSON 的全部選項（55題×4）、題幹、8 段選文逐字程式比對；pdftotext 與 docx 的英文 token 序列全文比對一致；以 Read 檢視題本 PDF 第1–8頁影像確認段落、畫底線字與空格位置。
issues: 無統計資料、無評分原則：units.json 中 86 學年度只有題本（PDF、Word）與選擇題答案，沒有 stats（答對率／鑑別度／選項分析）與 scoring 檔，所有小題 stats 為 null，sources.scoring／stats 為空陣列（validator 的「整份考卷沒有任何統計資料」warning 屬實）。
答案檔（answer.pdf）為國文、英文、數學合併的掃描影像（第1頁「八十六學年學科能力測驗國文考科、英文考科及數學考科答案」，第2頁為社會、自然），無文字層；以 pdftoppm 250dpi 轉圖、裁切英文欄放大，用 Read 看影像逐題抄錄第1–55題，每題答案皆與題意核對一致。
簡答題第1–5題：大考中心未公布簡答題參考答案或評分原則（答案檔只有選擇題），answer／accepted_answers／scoring_notes 均填 null。英文作文亦無官方評分原則，answer 為 null。
非選擇題題號：簡答題題本印為 1.–5.，與選擇題第1–5題重號，因此 no 保留 1–5、label 改為「簡答1」–「簡答5」；英文作文題本未編號，no 填 1、label 為「作文」（同 gsat-87／88／89 慣例）。validator 的「題號重複 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]」warning 因此產生，屬合理。

結構核對：gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 83–87 期別只有粗略描述（「86單一選擇題55題」、非選擇題兩大題），與本卷一致。本卷實際結構：第一部分 單一選擇題—壹、詞彙與語法 1–15（每題1分，15分）、貳、片語 16–20（每題1分，5分）、參、綜合測驗 21–40（每題1分，20分）、肆、閱讀測驗 41–55（每題2分，30分）；第二部分 非選擇題—壹、簡答題 5題×2分（10分）、貳、英文作文（20分）；合計100分，考試時間100分鐘（封面）。各大題標題題本未印配分百分比，points_total 依說明文字「每題答對得1分／2分」「每題2分，共10分」「共20分」計算。part 依題本「第一部分：單一選擇題」「第二部分：非選擇題」填「單一選擇題」「非選擇題」。

貳、片語（第16–20題）為「選出與劃線部份語意最接近的字詞」的單句同義替換題，題本另立一大題，依 schema 歸為 vocabulary（s2，獨立於 s1）；題幹中畫底線的片語以 <u>…</u> 標出（on purpose、stands for、gave rise to、appeals to、came to）。tags.test_point 為 phrase，answer_pos 為正確選項的詞性，key_phrase 為畫底線片語的原形。
題本原文疑誤，逐字保留：(1) 貳、片語的說明寫「第11至20題」，實際為第16至20題；且答案卡位置寫「選擇題答案區」，與其他大題的「選擇題第一部分」不同。(2) 第20題選項 (A)「Rose」首字母大寫（其餘選項小寫），PDF 與 Word 版相同。

空格與空白正規化：詞彙題空格一律寫成 ______，前後各留一個空格、標點前不留空格（第2題題本為「own ______ , please」標點前多一空格、第4題為「more______?」空格緊貼前字，皆屬排版，已正規化）；第3題空格在題本位於行末（「had been ______ engaged」），Word 版底線 run 證實位置。綜合測驗第34題題本為「[[34]]some minutes」（底線緊貼後一字），已補一個空格。句間兩個空白一律改為一個。

段落：第31–40題選文第4段在 Word 版拆成兩段（[[37]] … rejected. 與 [[38]] He was a victim …），但 PDF 影像中 [[38]] 那一行未縮排、緊接上一行，屬同一段，passage 合併為一段。第21–25題選文第3行在 pdftotext 因左右對齊被拆成逐字母（s m o o t h l y …），以 Word 版與影像確認為「smoothly and quietly」。第52–55題選文首段（Penghu, Nov.24— 電頭）在題本不縮排、電頭為粗體；簡答題選文第2段「The old sages…」題本亦不縮排；passage 皆以換行分段，不保留縮排。
